plan.title: Paired 3-condition blood RNA-seq DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: Four subjects each contribute a control, treated_a, and treated_b blood sample (12 samples, 12000 genes, raw Salmon gene counts, single batch). The within-subject pairing across three conditions is the central design feature: subject variation must be blocked to isolate the treatment effect. The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 paired multi-group procedure: (1) sample-structure QC via blind VST/PCA/distance heatmap to confirm subjects and conditions behave as expected and to catch mislabeling or outliers before modeling; (2) a minimal low-count pre-filter; (3) a DESeq2 model with design ~ subject + condition, size-factor normalization internal to the model; (4) an omnibus likelihood-ratio test (full ~subject+condition vs reduced ~subject) to find genes responding to EITHER treatment within-subject, followed by three named pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_a vs treated_b) with control as the explicit reference level, answering both halves of the research question (which genes respond to either treatment, and whether the two treatments differ from each other); (5) ashr shrinkage of each contrast's log2 fold change (ashr rather than apeglm because the treated_a-vs-treated_b contrast is not a single model coefficient); (6) BH multiple-testing correction within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering; (7) per-contrast fgsea preranked enrichment on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome/WikiPathways (follow-up), all staged locally for human; (8) a consolidated report with fit diagnostics, reproducibility record, and explicit caveats. The design has only 4 subjects (fixed subject block, no random-effect alternative needed) and one batch, so no batch correction step is required.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap

~ subject + condition, reference level = control, explicit factor releveling
DESeq2 LRT (full ~subject+condition vs reduced ~subject) to find any-treatment effect, then pairwise Wald contrasts treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_a vs treated_b
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast, alpha=0.05, independent filtering on
fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald statistic per contrast, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome/WikiPathways
Combined DE + enrichment report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
